Definition: from G303 and G2240; to attain to, i.e. (figuratively) be proper:--convenient, be fit.
BiblicalUsage: Paul uses this word for what is fitting: filthiness and foolish talking are not convenient, and wives are to submit to their husbands as it is fit in the Lord. The word draws the line between what suits a Christian and what does not.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for what is fitting carries no doctrine of its own; its use is practical, that some speech and some behaviour simply do not suit people who belong to Christ.
